channel.title: Crypto Front Page
channel.description: Crypto Front Page reports news on Bitcoin, Ethereum, stablecoins, exchanges, DeFi protocols, regulation and network upgrades across the crypto industry.

item.title: What a Bridge Withdrawal Claim Does, Step by Step
item.description: A bridge withdrawal claim proves a Polygon burn was checkpointed and asks Ethereum to release the matching asset; the burn alone does not complete withdrawal.

item.title: Blast to wind down Ethereum layer 2 as costs exceed revenue
item.description: Blast will wind down its Ethereum Layer 2 after saying upkeep costs exceed revenue, with withdrawals paused during a Lido exit and the normal interface available until Oct. 26.

item.title: When to Revoke a Token Spending Approval
item.description: A token approval lets a contract move specified tokens later; revoke it when the job is done, the spender is unfamiliar, or its allowance exceeds what you need.

item.title: SEC proposes new crypto custody routes for advisers and funds
item.description: The SEC proposed new custody paths for advisers and funds, including conditional self-custody and state trust companies, with safeguards and a 60-day comment period.

item.title: BNY and Payward discuss broad financial infrastructure pact
item.description: BNY and Kraken parent Payward are discussing a broad services pact spanning custody, trading and payments, but the talks remain private and no deal is assured.

item.title: A Pending TRON Swap Needs a Lot Record Before It Settles
item.description: A pending TRON swap has no final tax lot until it executes; prepare the outgoing asset’s basis, transaction value, fee and receipt data before the chain settles it.

item.title: What Quote Expiry Does in a Crypto Swap
item.description: Quote expiry limits how long a displayed crypto swap price can be accepted, reducing stale-price risk while slippage and execution limits do separate work.

item.title: The Role of Intermediate Assets in Cross-Chain Swaps
item.description: Intermediate assets help a cross-chain route find liquidity, but each conversion adds costs and execution steps to review before you approve the swap.

item.title: Why BNB Chain Charts Can Continue Across Liquidity Pairs
item.description: BNB Chain token charts can continue across liquidity pairs, but each pool records its own trades; read the pair, quote asset and depth before comparing prices.

item.title: Buying Governance Tokens Before a Vote Closes
item.description: Buying before a vote closes does not always create voting power: check the proposal’s snapshot, delegation rules, token route and deadline before acting.

item.title: Reading Router Changes in Token Activity
item.description: A router change appears in the contract calls behind a swap, not in the token transfer alone; compare transaction paths to tell what changed and why.

item.title: Where Destination Gas Comes From in a Cross-Chain Message
item.description: A cross-chain message carries a destination gas budget; the protocol prices that work, subtracts a reserve from swap output, then broadcasts the call.

item.title: What to Do When an Ethereum Swap Is Pending
item.description: A pending Ethereum swap is an unconfirmed transaction, not a stuck exchange; check its status, fee, and nonce before waiting, replacing, or canceling it.

item.title: Why a Failed Chainflip Payout Can Still Be Recovered
item.description: A failed Chainflip payout can leave the transfer unsent while its signed payload remains available, giving the recipient a short window to broadcast it manually.

item.title: Compare impermanent loss with fees before adding liquidity
item.description: Impermanent loss is the value a liquidity position gives up against holding the same tokens; estimate price divergence, fee income and range behavior before depositing.

item.title: SEC grants conditional path for tokenized stock trading
item.description: The SEC granted five-year conditional relief for permissioned venues to trade tokenized U.S. stocks through blockchain liquidity pools, with investor safeguards.

item.title: Why a Failed Avalanche Swap Still Costs Gas
item.description: A failed Avalanche swap can leave token balances unchanged while charging for contract execution; a CEX order usually stays off chain until funds move.

item.title: Choose a Polygon Bridge route by its delivery steps
item.description: When minutes matter, compare Polygon bridge routes by delivery estimate, fees and asset support, then check the destination chain and what must happen after you send.

item.title: How Much BNB Chain Liquidity Does a Trade Need?
item.description: A BNB Chain pool has no universal minimum: compare your order with usable reserves, expected price impact, fees and sell-side depth before swapping.

item.title: SEC proposes custody framework for advisers and funds
item.description: The SEC proposed a custody framework for advisers and funds on Oct. 1, including conditional adviser-held keys and state trust companies, with public comments still to come.
